source_text: Revelatur ira Dei de caelo in omnem impietatem et iniustitiam hominum qui veritatem in iniustitia detinent. Propterea tradidit illos Deus in desideria cordis, in passiones ignominiae, in reprobum sensum. Gloria Christo. Amen.
orientation: Origen is quoting Paul's words from Romans 1 about God's wrath being revealed against human unrighteousness.
pass_a_gloss: [It] is revealed [the] wrath of God from heaven against all impiety and injustice of men who the truth in injustice hold down. Therefore handed over them God into [the] desires of [the] heart, into [the] passions of shame, into [a] reprobate mind. Glory [to] Christ. Amen.

choices.why: The glossary bans 'justice' for iustitia Dei, and this is the negative counterpart; 'unrighteousness' keeps the moral-legal sense of iniustitia as the opposite of God's righteousness.
Reprobus means rejected or worthless; 'reprobate mind' is the standard rendering and preserves the passive sense of being rejected by God.
Ignominia means disgrace or shame; 'passions of disgrace' keeps the genitive relation and the sense of shameful passions.
Trado means to hand over or deliver; 'handed over' preserves the judicial sense of God giving them up to their own desires.

pass_b_english: The wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all impiety and unrighteousness of people who hold the truth in unrighteousness (Romans 1:18). Therefore God handed them over to the desires of their heart, to passions of disgrace, to a reprobate mind (Romans 1:24, 26, 28). Glory to Christ. Amen.
